reviews.text: I am very grateful for the services of both the clinic and the hotel, as they are close to my home. The doctor treats me with care, sometimes strictly, sometimes gently. The staff are also friendly. They have kindly addressed my urgent concerns. I am very thankful.

Looking at the reviews sorted by worst to newest, it seems this place is still doing the same old things.

I switched to a clinic near Roppongi Hills. It's inexpensive, the staff are kind, and they have extensive clinical experience; I'm very satisfied.

Is it a fee for the location? While some animal hospitals occasionally charge double the usual price, this is an astonishingly high amount.

I considered going because it's nearby, but if that's the case, I'll go to the most famous and trustworthy hospital in Japan, where I've had surgeries and simple procedures done before. That hospital charges the same as other hospitals, has state-of-the-art equipment, and their animal treatment experience is incredibly high. I'm disappointed.
I was stunned when they asked me, "Our prices are high, is that okay?" and then I was taken aback when they explained that it would cost over 20,000 yen, including the initial consultation fee.

I've been to this vet several times, but when my dog ​​stopped eating due to a sprained ankle, they just poked his ear, declared it an allergy, and sold me dog food.

It didn't solve anything, and it didn't alleviate my anxiety and worry about my beloved pet, who is more important to me than my own life.

Every other word was injection or food change. It seemed like they were only interested in profit. I'm willing to spend any amount of money to address my dog's changes, but I felt like I was just being exploited by a brazen veterinarian's profit-driven diagnosis and sales tactics.

It's extremely unpleasant. If I can't forgive them, I honestly don't want anyone from this hospital to touch my dog ​​ever again.
Pet owners, please come and talk to us. Our doctors will listen to your concerns with compassion. If you have any problems, please come to us.

My rescued toy poodle, Caramel (estimated age 9-11), was diagnosed with a malignant melanoma.

As the tumor was in his mouth, another hospital asked me to decide whether to have him undergo surgery to remove his right lower jaw immediately.

I couldn't make a decision right then and there, and while I was debating what to do, they referred me to All Pet Clinic, where I made an appointment for an afternoon appointment. They told me he only had a few months to live if we didn't perform the surgery, but even if we did, if it had spread to his lungs, it would recur... Even though they told me the same thing, they took the time to carefully explain what was going to happen next and to me, taking my dog ​​and I into consideration.

My mind was blank and I was still wondering what to do, but two days later, the director called me and asked if I wanted a CT scan. I was touched by their concern, and the thought that there was a possibility of him getting the surgery helped me change my mindset and think, "It's okay if he ends up sticking his tongue out!" So I decided to have the surgery to remove his right lower jaw.
As a result, Caramel struggled to eat at first after the surgery... but seeing him regain his normal eating habits made me truly glad I had the surgery. Since then, he's had various illnesses, including Cushing's disease, but the melanoma never recurred. As a result, we were able to spend about four years together after the melanoma. He passed away suddenly at home.

Caramel was saved by the director's surgery, and I'm so grateful that we were able to spend so much time together.

Since then, all of my dogs have been treated by the director at All Pet Clinic.

When my dog ​​friends ask me if there's a good hospital, I have no hesitation in recommending All Pet Clinic, and in fact, they still go there. Some people may think that the director's words are harsh, but I believe they're for the dog's sake and are speaking from the dog's perspective.


When my dog ​​friends tell me that they can't figure out what illness their dog has no matter where they go, I always suggest they try All Pet Clinic; it's the best hospital for me. Please continue to take good care of my Coconut and Chelsea and our other dog friends. 
The photos of Caramel are from 5 hours and 4 months before he went to the Rainbow Bridge. Thank you so much for all your help! Thank you so much⑅︎◡̈︎*

There's no other hospital that identifies pets by name and replies to them like that (lol). Is their goal to make pet owners uncomfortable?

The rude hospital director called a pet owner "mentally ill" in a reply to a review.

Although it's now gone, didn't he write that he "received support for developmental disabilities as a child"?

He's admitting that he's the one with a mental illness (lol).
Not only is his treatment of pet owners heartless, but he also has no love for animals whatsoever.

I also had a bad experience and switched hospitals.

This hospital has become like this since Dr. Horimoto, the female doctor, retired. The receptionist also seems to have learned from the director, and her service has also deteriorated.

My dogs have all been cared for here over the years.

They prioritize the animals, and while they sometimes give tough advice, they also empathize with the feelings of worried pet owners.

The facilities are excellent, which I also appreciate.

Until we moved, we had our tortoises and guinea pigs treated at this animal hospital.

I think this is the only hospital that treats exotic animals.

Previously, our tortoise completely stopped eating, and we went to another animal hospital and gave it IV fluids daily for about six months. Since the tortoise still wouldn't eat, we took it to All Pet Clinic. They performed surgery to allow liquid food to be directly delivered to its stomach via a catheter, and the tortoise started eating again about a week after the surgery.

The price is a little higher than other animal hospitals, but considering the well-being of our beloved pets, I don't think it's a problem.

They also provide thorough examinations for animals other than exotic animals. The fact that they communicate via LINE is very helpful.

We have been receiving care for our barn owl at this clinic for about eight years. Since there are few hospitals that treat this animal, we are truly grateful and rely on this clinic.

Thanks to Dr. Hirabayashi's appropriate advice, a calcium deficiency found during a health checkup was corrected, and our owl is now healthy and happy.

Pet owls are still relatively uncommon, and there are many unknown aspects to them. Therefore, even small things can cause anxiety for owners, but we are truly grateful to the doctor who treats these rare animals and their owners with such kindness and care, despite their busy schedules.

Furthermore, this hospital's boarding service is excellent; they take great care of our owl, who is not very tame, so we can entrust him to them with peace of mind.

We will continue to rely on the doctor, nurses, and staff for the care of both our owl and ourselves. Thank you very much.
He is a great teacher.

In 2025, a pre-vaccination consultation will be mandatory for rabies vaccinations, costing 15,000 yen for a 30-minute slot.

In 2022, my previous dog contracted rabies and was treated here, but I received expensive tests without receiving appropriate treatment, hence this rating (after transferring to another clinic, a diagnosis was made immediately, and treatment was provided by a trusted veterinarian, but sadly, my dog ​​crossed the rainbow bridge. I regret not being able to start treatment sooner).

When I first visited a few years ago, there was a kind female veterinarian, and I felt very relaxed, so I gave it a 5-star rating and recommended it to everyone. However, I can't recommend it now; I don't know about other animals, but I certainly wouldn't recommend it for birds. During the restraint, they grabbed my bird with a thick towel, and I heard cries of disgust I'd never heard before. Both the bird and I left feeling very uncomfortable.

When asked about the room temperature for the bird's enclosure, I answered 27-28 degrees Celsius, but they persistently asked if it was 27 or 28 degrees, and then asked what wattage the UV lamp was. How could I possibly remember that? It was such a strange question; why ask such a thing? When I asked a counter-question, it turned out they were trying to recommend a thermometer that could continuously measure temperature to within 0.1 degrees and display a temperature graph. If that's the case, they should have explained the functions of such a convenient device and recommended a suitable temperature setting. Similarly, they should have recommended the manufacturer and wattage of the UV lamp before recommending it. I think it's wrong to test whether I could answer and then act condescendingly when I couldn't.

This teacher might have a strong need for one-upmanship, validation, and attention. Other people's comments might be helpful.

We've been using this hospital since we first got our pet, and now we have two dogs, and we trust it completely as our regular care center. Dr. Hirabayashi always puts animals first, and his examinations and explanations are thorough and reliable. My oldest dog underwent patellar surgery, but he received thorough post-operative care and is now running around without any problems.
We are also grateful that we can leave our pets in the safe and secure environment of a hospital while we're away, even for long periods of time. They send us photos and videos and keep us updated on their progress so we don't have to worry about anything. We couldn't ask for a more reliable place to leave our family members.
We are also truly grateful to the staff, who are always so kind and willing to answer even the smallest of questions.
Our dogs often stop by on their walks; it's more than just a hospital; it's a place of peace and security for them, with doctors and staff they trust and love.
We look forward to continuing to rely on you as our lifelong family doctor.

I think it's been 7 years since I started going there! The clinic has always been incredibly clean, and the staff are always so kind.

Every time, they give me precise advice and explain in detail what's needed and what treatment should be performed. Of course, they never force anything; they only do what's possible, so I feel very confident leaving my dog ​​in their care. I sometimes rely on them too much, though! I often consult with them via LINE, and their quick responses are a great help! My dog ​​is getting older and gets anxious about even the smallest things, so I end up asking a lot of basic questions, but they always listen and understand my feelings as a pet owner. I'm always grateful for their flexible and adaptable approach. I'd like to continue going there in the future! 🐶♡

I started keeping rabbits and was looking for a veterinary clinic that could treat exotic animals, which is how I found this clinic (I inquired at several other clinics, but they seemed to only treat rabbits as an extension of dogs and cats). When my rabbit was a baby, I rushed him in alone with a pet sheet that looked like it had blood in his urine, but it turned out he had eaten too many carrots. Since then, I've received advice on feeding, cage setup, and other aspects of rabbit care, and thanks to them, my rabbit has grown into a perfectly healthy rabbit.

The veterinarian here takes the time to talk to each patient individually, making other clinics feel like an assembly line. They truly care for both the animals and the owners. Many exotic animal clinics seem to have strong personalities, but the head veterinarian here is not overbearing, and their treatment plan is clear, taking into account the animals' well-being, so I trust them completely. They also show me case photos and medical books, and I've gained a lot of knowledge through our conversations; they've really helped me grow as a pet owner! (laughs)

Above all, I think their skills and facilities are outstanding.

My rabbit was spayed when she was still very young, but I think it's rare to find a veterinarian who can perform tracheal intubation and anesthesia on a rabbit weighing less than 1 kg. I really want pet owners who are hesitant about surgery due to the risks of anesthesia to know about this hospital.

They also have a CT scanner for small animals that can be used without anesthesia, which is helpful because it allows for less stressful medical treatment.

The price is higher than local hospitals, but I think it's reasonable for the reasons mentioned above.

The head veterinarian is a wonderful person who has also been involved in pet rescue during earthquakes! I think they should spread the word more.

We've known Dr. Hirabayashi for over 13 years, ever since he was in Asakusa. Although it's far now, we still travel from Chiba Prefecture to this hospital.

The hospital has a wonderful atmosphere, and we always feel refreshed after our appointments.

The head veterinarian's approach to animals is truly sincere and reliable; as a pet owner, I feel completely at ease entrusting my beloved dog to him. He thoroughly explains the tests and symptoms, and I'm always grateful for his professional and attentive service. For our family, All Pet Clinic is the only animal hospital we consider. The reason is Dr. Hirabayashi.

My dog ​​is getting older. We look forward to your continued support. We rely on you!

I have been using your services for seven years now to care for my beloved dog.

He has had a sensitive stomach since he was a puppy, which has caused him to get sick many times and require him to be tested for allergies, so I have been using your services for a long time.

The doctor is very knowledgeable and we consult on a wide range of issues, from illnesses to health support and anti-aging measures.

At times, I see him use strong language in important situations, but it is clear that this is because he truly cares about animals.

I was also very grateful for the detailed support I received via LINE when I was out and about, or when I returned home with my dog ​​to give birth, and for the online consultations I was able to get.

I have nothing but gratitude for Director Hirabayashi,
so this is going to be a long message.
I first saw him when he was in Taito Ward and have been receiving his care for about 10 years.
I have decided to ask him for all surgical care.
I had my skin examined many times at a nearby hospital, but it didn't get any better. But with Director's accurate diagnosis,
my skin condition has improved dramatically.

I don't think there is another doctor who puts animals first as much. This hospital makes me realize the importance of what pet owners should do for their pets.
Thank you to the veterinary nurses and staff for taking the time to help me despite your busy schedules.

He moved from his previous hospital, and I came with him to this one.

This is his fourth dog, so we've been working together for nearly 20 years.

He's a very loving doctor when it comes to animals.

That's why I think he can be harsh on owners at times...
Is that why?
The reviews are so divided between 1 and 5.
Hmm. That's a shame.

I've never heard him say anything abusive.

I'm sure it depends on the person you're with, but he always puts the animals first and explains things kindly and carefully.
When costs are involved, he prioritizes the owners' opinions and thoughts.

After the Great East Japan Earthquake, he set up a shelter, and I've seen him visit Fukushima many times.

He's still involved in animal protection work, and one of my dogs was given to me through one of his services.

Seeing how the reviews were so divided, I decided to share my thoughts.

I've been a patient of the clinic director for many years, and I always feel completely at ease entrusting my beloved family member to their care.

They treat a wide range of animals, from dogs and cats to small animals and even rare species. They are always compassionate and attentive, and they have the latest medical equipment, allowing them to carefully propose the best treatment plan for each animal at any given time. I have complete confidence in this clinic.

The staff are all cheerful and kind, and they even send updates via LINE when my pet is hospitalized, which gives me peace of mind even when I'm away. They also offer suggestions for supplements and lifestyle advice to prevent illness, which is very helpful for daily health management.

This is a wonderful animal hospital that truly cares for both animals and their owners.

We have two cats under their care. We have been treating them since they were born, and the clinic director, Dr. Hirabayashi, is caring, polite, knowledgeable, and very dedicated. He also provides treatment and advice that is very considerate of us as pet owners. There is no other place where we can leave our family members with more peace of mind than Dr. Hirabayashi and his staff. We plan to continue to receive their care for many years to come.
There is no other clinic where we would entrust our cats’ lives to.
The doctor is deeply committed to learning, highly responsible, and filled with genuine love for animals.
They provide care that truly supports both the pet and the owner, always approaching treatment with compassion and dedication.

The director has a very condescending attitude... who does he think he is? I've taken my dog ​​there three times, and although I'm a layman when it comes to symptoms and disease names, I've looked them up online and thought I had some knowledge. I couldn't stand the way he talked down to me, so I went to this clinic because it was convenient and close by, but I thought it would be better for my dog ​​if I went to a doctor I could trust, even if it was far away.

We are always so grateful for your care regarding our Japanese quail.

We first met Dr. Hirabayashi when one of our two quail was suffering from egg binding and was very weak. Unfortunately, that quail did not survive, but I vividly remember how kindly Dr. Hirabayashi and the staff treated us during our initial consultation, when we were very upset.

Since then, we have been regularly taking our remaining quail for checkups. They are small animals and prone to illness, but Dr. Hirabayashi's diagnoses are incredibly accurate, and after taking the prescribed medication, they become energetic as if by magic. He also readily sees them when they suddenly become ill, and we truly rely on him.

We are also deeply grateful for the extensive support we receive, not just the medical care. At the pet hotel, even though the staff are busy, they keep us updated with photos and videos, which gives us peace of mind. Furthermore, if we have any concerns about daily care, we can immediately consult with them via LINE, which is incredibly reassuring.


Actually, due to my husband's work, our Japanese quail has moved to a southern island, but the doctor has continued to provide support online, saying, "Don't worry, I can still see you remotely!" I was deeply touched by how kind and caring this doctor is towards both animals and their owners.

When saying goodbye to a pet, owners surely have many regrets. But because we have such caring doctors and staff, we can cherish the time we have with our pet with peace of mind. Thank you so much.
They will listen to your concerns with genuine care.

We've been going to this vet since our dog was a puppy. We started going because it happened to be close to our house, but when I called before our first visit, they explained the relatively high initial consultation fee and the reasons behind it in detail. I hesitated at first, but after the examination, I understood the reasons and was convinced, so I decided to go ahead with it.

The consultation time, during which they carefully explained everything to a novice owner with little knowledge, ended up being over an hour long. I remember being surprised that they spent more than an hour with each patient. There are many animal hospitals, and it's difficult to compare, but I think a vet who takes such thorough care of each patient is very valuable. And because we've been going there for so long, you can feel that they're anticipating what our dog will need as he gets older. If there are no health problems, we sometimes don't go for a check-up for six months, but being able to get prescriptions just for that is helpful because knowing what medications to keep on hand allows me to control the situation as an owner.

I've been putting into practice what I learned from when my dog ​​was a puppy, and even though I didn't know what was right myself, now that he's two and a half years old, when we go to the grooming salon or daycare, the owner is often complimented on how well he's been groomed and cared for. That's when I really started to realize that following the doctor's advice was the right thing to do. There are all sorts of opinions out there, but I think finding the right hospital and doctor for you is really important. I want to continue using their services, and if I have any friends who are getting puppies like me, I would definitely recommend them. When I'm away for extended periods, I prioritize peace of mind and use their boarding service. When I visit the boarding facility, the staff dotes on my dog, and he's grown to like the hospital, so I recommend it to dogs that are afraid of the vet!
